dispositions.topic_text: Installation and production-admission verification of the first-release AGENTS.md writer rule
dispositions.what: R0-96 requires the room-name and alias rule (purpose and number; no person, nor a person's condition, health, age or need; alias a neutral label of at most 40 characters) in the agent's instructions on the home server (Factory platform/home_server/workspace/AGENTS.md, installed into /srv/cabinet-agent/) before Registry's first release goes into production. Deployment verifies that the installed release carries it (Factory PR #261) before the first release serves Kernel. Its absence blocks no write in Registry: without a standing approval each room the agent adds waits for the owner's approval of its exact request, name included (R0-99, K-08); under a standing approval the instructions are the only protection (R0-96).
keeps:
In the first release the agent learns it from its instructions, which the platform installs in the agent's home on the home server (Factory
`platform/home_server/workspace/AGENTS.md`); adding the rule there is the platform's change, made before the first release goes into production.
options: Bake the governed AGENTS.md into the platform release or VM Agent image.
Provision the versioned Factory file during deployment and fail admission if the required rule is absent or stale.
Mount the Factory file read-only at runtime and require the mount at agent startup.
Verify both the generated source artifact in factory checks and the installed copy during deployment.
consequences: Baking couples instruction changes to release or image rebuilds.
Provisioning permits ordinary updates but requires version and installed-copy checks.
A runtime mount preserves one source of truth but makes startup depend on the mount.
Factory and deployment checks together cover artifact creation and the production installation boundary.

dispositions.topic_text: Manifest and operation-contract encoding for withdrawal without idempotency and with refused replays
dispositions.what: R0-99: withdrawing a pointer names the pointer only and carries no idempotency key; a repeated withdrawal is refused as withdrawing a pointer already withdrawn (Primary actions, R0-14). State 5 states it in the withdraw operation's public API and in Registry's derived manifest record: no idempotency-key input, effect class state-transition, replay behaviour 'a repeat is refused'; while adding a room and publishing a pointer carry their request id as the idempotency key (A01, R0-88).
keeps:
Withdrawing a pointer makes nothing; it names the
pointer only and carries no idempotency key, and a repeated withdrawal is
refused as withdrawing a pointer already withdrawn (Primary actions, R0-14).
Its replay behaviour in the manifest record is that a repeat is refused.
options: Omit the idempotency-key field and use an explicit replay-behavior value for refusal.
Represent the idempotency-key field as null and describe the refusal in the failure contract.
Represent replay refusal solely as a typed operation failure, with no separate replay field.
Use a shared write schema that forbids the idempotency field for withdrawal and declares an already-withdrawn failure.
consequences: An explicit replay value gives Kernel a direct machine-readable guarantee but requires that value in the manifest vocabulary.
A null field preserves a uniform shape but creates a distinct null-versus-omitted contract state.
A failure-only representation requires consumers to derive replay semantics from the failure contract.
A shared schema reduces variation but needs an exact forbidden-field rule.
